title: Rahti project configuration
description: The project's single source of truth. Settings are yours to edit; `schema`, `createdWith` and `scaffold` are written by the scaffold and read by the upgrade command.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema, so an editor can offer completion and validation.

schema.description: The configuration shape this file is written for. A build refuses a file claiming a higher number than it understands, rather than reading a key it would get wrong.

createdWith.description: The Rahti version that scaffolded this project. Provenance, not a constraint: the version actually in use is the one in Cargo.toml.

app.description: Where the file-system router and the static files live.

dir.description: Root of the file-system router, relative to the crate root. Every page.rs, layout.rs and route.rs below it becomes a URL.

public.description: Static files, relative to the working directory the server runs in. Its *contents* are served from `/`: public/css/styles.css becomes /css/styles.css. Override at runtime with RAHTI_PUBLIC_DIR.

server.description: The address the compiled binary listens on. A deployment overrides it from the environment: PORT wins over server.port, HOST over server.host.

host.description: Bind address, unless the HOST environment variable names another. The default wildcard answers on every interface, which is what a container needs; narrow it to 127.0.0.1 to keep a development server off the local network.

port.description: Bind port, unless the PORT environment variable names another.

css.description: The stylesheet build. Nothing here is required: with no `css` object and no entry file, the build does not change.

engine.description: How `entry` becomes `output`. "tailwind" compiles it with the Tailwind standalone CLI. "plain" copies it as it is — no CLI, no download, no network. "none" leaves `output` alone so you manage the public directory yourself. Under every engine you edit `entry` and the browser is served `output`, so switching is one word, not a migration.

entry.description: The stylesheet you edit, relative to the crate root. Compiled, copied, or ignored according to `engine`. Built only if it exists.

output.description: Where the compiled sheet lands. Under the public directory so it is served, and checked in so a clone with no CLI still has one.

version.description: Which Tailwind standalone CLI release to use. Pinned rather than floating: a stylesheet that changes because upstream released is not wanted.

download.description: Fetch the CLI when it is not already in .rahti/bin/, on PATH, or named by RAHTI_TAILWIND. Off by default: a build script that reaches the network unasked breaks --offline, vendored trees and sandboxed CI, and the committed stylesheet means nothing is lost by waiting to be asked.

minify.description: Compress the output. A setting rather than a profile switch on purpose: `output` is committed, so tying it to the build profile would have release and debug builds committing the file back and forth forever.

sha256.description: Expected hash of the downloaded CLI, one entry per platform — a checksum is of one specific binary, so a team on mixed machines needs an entry each. A platform with no entry downloads unverified and the build prints its hash to paste in. Once listed, a binary that stops matching is refused rather than run.

ws.description: The project uses WebSockets: its Cargo.toml carries the `ws` feature on the `rahti` dependency, which is what compiles `rahti::ws` and the `#[socket]` attribute. Absent means no — the same reading as an absent `db`. The build itself never needs this key (a `#[socket]` in the tree is what wires the endpoint); it exists so `cargo rahti upgrade` knows the manifest is expected to carry the feature, and can say precisely what to add when it does not.

mcp.description: The project opts into Rahti's MCP developer tooling. When true, the scaffold owns .mcp.json, which launches the separately installed `rahti-mcp` server against this project. It does not add an application dependency or expose an HTTP route. Absent means no.

db.description: The database wiring. Absent — or null — means the project has no database: no directories are created, no modules are generated, and nothing in the build mentions SeaORM. Note what is *not* here: the connection string. It carries credentials and this file is committed, so the URL is read from DATABASE_URL at runtime and lives in an ignored .env.

backend.description: Which engine the application talks to. Recorded rather than inferred from the connection string, because the string is not in this file to read. It decides one thing — the `sea-orm` feature your Cargo.toml needs (sqlx-sqlite, sqlx-postgres, sqlx-mysql) — and is otherwise only used to make a message name the right engine. A misspelling is refused rather than defaulted: falling back to SQLite would wire a database nobody is talking to.

models.description: Where the entities live, relative to the crate root. A flat directory: one file per table, named after it in snake_case. `mod.rs` is generated from the contents — the entities themselves are yours, and Rahti neither writes nor reads SeaORM code.

migrations.description: Where the migrations live, relative to the crate root. `mod.rs` is generated and carries the `Migrator`, which lists every file here in filename order — so name a migration mYYYYMMDD_NNNNNN_<what>.rs and adding the file is the whole of adding the migration. A migration written but never pushed into a hand-maintained list is the quietest failure there is: the file exists, the table does not, and nothing says why.

scaffold.description: What the scaffold wrote, and the SHA-256 of each file at the moment it was written. The upgrade command compares these to decide whether a file is still its own to change: a hash that matches may be rewritten or removed silently, one that differs is yours and is left alone with a note. This is why an upgrade can retire a feature without ever destroying work.
